**Question.** Yes if Sergey Lavrov is publicly reported to be physically on the ground in Florida between 1 and 31 December 2026. The realistic route is the G20 leaders' summit at Trump National Doral, near Miami, on 14-15 December.

**Starting point.** Putin has not attended a G20 summit in person since 2019. Since 2022 Lavrov has led Russia's delegation three times out of four (Bali 2022, New Delhi 2023, Rio 2024); for Johannesburg 2025 the Kremlin sent Maxim Oreshkin instead. When Putin does travel to a major summit, Lavrov almost always travels with him.

**Recent evidence.**
- Russia will attend 'at a high level', but the head of delegation is not yet chosen (Foreign Ministry envoy Marat Berdyev to Izvestia, via TASS, 24 November). Peskov said the same day that no decision has been made on Putin, although Trump repeated his invitation in Shenzhen (TASS, 19 November).
- Putin sounded lukewarm on 19 November: he said his decision rests on 'what's happening in the country' and that Russia would be represented at a high level whatever his own plans (Open magazine with ANI).
- Lavrov is in the team that deals with Washington and can enter the US: he led the delegation at the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta on 30-31 October (TASS, Al Jazeera), and he sat in Putin's talks with Trump in Shenzhen (bne IntelliNews, 19 November).

**Estimate.** Putin attends in person: about 25%, and Lavrov would then come with him about 95% of the time. If Putin stays away (75%), Lavrov leads or joins the delegation about 65% of the time; otherwise an Oreshkin-style substitute, the prime minister or another official goes. About 2% covers a moved or cancelled summit. 0.98 x (0.25 x 0.95 + 0.75 x 0.65) = 0.71. Any other December trip to Florida adds well under 1%.

**What would give No.** Putin stays home and the Kremlin again names someone other than Lavrov, as in 2025; or the summit moves, or Russia downgrades its presence after a rupture with Washington.

**Forecast: 70%.**
